Description: Assumes features are continuous and follow a normal (Gaussian) distribution.
Typical Use Cases: Medical test values, sensor measurements, continuous numeric datasets.
Key Benefits: Works well with continuous data, simple & fast, requires fewer data points.

Description: Assumes features are counts (frequency of words/events). Uses multinomial distribution.
Typical Use Cases: Text classification (spam detection, topic modeling, sentiment analysis).
Key Benefits: Naturally handles word counts, great for high-dimensional data, strong in NLP tasks.

Description: Assumes features are binary (yes/no, 0/1). Uses Bernoulli distribution.
Typical Use Cases: Document classification (presence/absence of words), sentiment classification, recommendation with binary features.
Key Benefits: Useful when frequency doesn’t matter, handles sparse binary data, simpler representation in NLP tasks.
